newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's opposition turns up heat over budget.
newsitem.headline: Italy's opposition turns up heat over budget.

text.p: Former Italian prime minister Silvio Berlusconi on Thursday stepped up opposition to the government's 1997 budget plan, saying it would push Italy into a recession.
"We are very worried...we are becoming more convinced that this budget will not bring us to Europe (monetary union), but will hit the economy bringing us to recession," Berlusconi said.
He spoke at a news conference after a meeting of leaders of his centre-right Freedom Alliance, the opposition to Prime Minister Romano Prodi's centre-left government.
Berlusconi, who served as prime minister for eight months in 1994, said the Freedom Alliance was considering staging a demonstration against Prodi's 1997 budget on November 9.

He said they had drafted a letter to President Oscar Luigi Scalfaro complaining about provisions in the budget which would authorise certain taxes before the government showed how they would be administered.

"(The letter) is a warning of the fact that with dozens and dozens of these provisions, parliament runs the risk of not being able to discuss knowledgeably the particulars of what the government intends to do with regard to the budget," hard-right leader Gianfranco Fini said.
Prodi's budget aims to cut next year's deficit by 62.5 trillion lire ($42 billion). The package is weighted towards increased tax revenues with less emphasis on spending cuts.
Prodi has said tough budget measures were necessary if Italy wanted to make the grade for membership of Europe's planned single currency.
The package faces its first test in the Chamber of Deputies (lower house), where Prodi depends on support of the hard-left Communist Refoundation which is outside his coalition.
The Chamber will begin debate on Wednesday with a final vote expected by November 14. It then passes to the Senate.
Prodi also faces problems over the budget from the country's three main trades union confederations, CGIL, CISL and UIL.
Union leaders said they were not satisfied with answers to their questions about the budget at talks with Prodi on Thursday. Prodi convened another meeting with the unions for next Monday.
